title: Transport of a normalized tensor comparison and descent of its signed coherence
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal D,S)$ be ringed sites small relative to a common universe of ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ be a geometric morphism, with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits and a homomorphism of commutative ring sheaves $u^{-1}R\to S$. Put $F(M)=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and assume $F$ exact. Use unbounded derived categories with localization functors $q_R,q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A resolving complex means a K-flat complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

Let $L=Lu^*$ have its canonical natural comparison $\epsilon$ and resolving-model isomorphisms $e_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $U=D(F)$ with $\kappa_A:U(q_RA)\cong q_S(FA)$ and all integer shift comparisons $s_{n,K}:U(K[n])\cong(UK)[n]$ from exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Assume that $F$ preserves flat sheaves, resolving complexes and small direct sums, and let a shift-compatible natural isomorphism $\eta:L\cong U$ be given with $\kappa_P\eta_{q_RP}=e_P$ on every resolving $P$.

Use the actual K-flat derived tensors and representative isomorphisms $r_{E,G}:q_RT(E,G)\cong q_RE\otimes_R^Lq_RG$ and $r'$ over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Here $T$ is signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $c_{E,G}:FT(E,G)\cong T(FE,FG)$ be the canonical cochain pullback comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], with local formulas $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ and inverse $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)\mapsto st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. Let $\mu^L$ be the normalized canonical tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit]. Define
$$\mu_{K,H}=(\eta_K\otimes\eta_H)\mu^L_{K,H}\eta_{K\otimes_R^LH}^{-1}.$$
Then $\mu$ is a natural isomorphism and, for every resolving pair $E,G$ and $V=T(E,G)$, it satisfies
$$(\kappa_E\otimes\kappa_G)\mu_{q_RE,q_RG}U(r_{E,G})=r'_{FE,FG}q_S(c_{E,G})\kappa_V.$$
It is the unique natural transformation $U(-\otimes_R^L-)\to U(-)\otimes_S^LU(-)$ with these representative components.

Let $t,t'$ be the composite two-variable total-shift comparisons normalized by $(-1)^{bp}$ on original first-factor degree $p$, with the same order of extracting the shifts over both rings [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. Let $\alpha,\alpha'$ and $\sigma,\sigma'$ be the derived reassociation and symmetry comparisons normalized on resolving total models by unsigned reassociation and $(-1)^{pq}$ on bidegree $(p,q)$, respectively. For arbitrary unbounded $K,H,N\in D(R)$ and all integers $a,b$ one has
$$t'_{a,b}(s_{a,K}\otimes s_{b,H})\mu_{K[a],H[b]}=\mu_{K,H}[a+b]s_{a+b,K\otimes^LH}U(t_{a,b}),$$
$$\mu_{H,K}U(\sigma_{K,H})=\sigma'_{UK,UH}\mu_{K,H},$$
$$(1\otimes\mu_{H,N})\mu_{K,H\otimes^LN}U(\alpha_{K,H,N})=\alpha'_{UK,UH,UN}(\mu_{K,H}\otimes1)\mu_{K\otimes^LH,N}.$$
These are equations for the specified representative-normalized comparison; no boundedness is imposed on any input.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_R,\mathcal P_S$ be the resolving classes. Total tensors of resolving complexes are resolving by [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]; their integer shifts are resolving by [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated]. Thus $V=T(E,G)$, $T(V,J)$, $T(E,T(G,J))$ and the shifted inputs used below are legitimate computation models. The hypothesis on $F$ puts their images in $\mathcal P_S$. In particular all occurrences of $e$, $r$, $r'$ and $c$ below have the required hypotheses even for complexes unbounded in both directions.

Conjugating the natural isomorphism $\mu^L$ of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] by the given natural isomorphism $\eta$ gives a natural isomorphism $\mu$. On a resolving pair, naturality of $\eta$ at $r=r_{E,G}$ says $\eta_{q_RE\otimes^Lq_RG}^{-1}U(r)=L(r)\eta_{q_RV}^{-1}$. Insert this identity and $\kappa_P\eta_{q_RP}=e_P$ in the defining formula. The representative normalization of the cited node gives
$$(\kappa_E\otimes\kappa_G)\mu U(r)=(e_E\otimes e_G)\mu^L L(r)\eta_{q_RV}^{-1}=r'_{FE,FG}q_S(c_{E,G})e_V\eta_{q_RV}^{-1}=r'_{FE,FG}q_S(c_{E,G})\kappa_V.$$
Every cancellation is of a specified isomorphism; no choice of a tensor comparison on object values is used.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), normalized representative formula, transported along the given eta.

proof.text: Two natural transformations with the displayed representative components have equal restrictions to $\mathcal P_R\times\mathcal P_R$: cancel $\kappa_E\otimes\kappa_G$ and $U(r_{E,G})$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] then makes them equal on $D(R)\times D(R)$. This proves precisely the claimed uniqueness, with no restriction to morphisms represented by chain maps.

First check the simultaneous-shift equation on resolving $E,G$. Write $x\in E^i$, $y\in G^j$ with original degrees $i,j$. For the stated normalization extract the first shift $a$ first (unsigned), then the second shift $b$; [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] gives $(-1)^{bi}$. Termwise $F$ commutes with shifts by the degreewise-identity comparison, and its localization comparisons $\kappa,s$ respect this by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Substitute the representative square from step 2 into both sides, using the naturality of $r,r'$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. After conjugating by these representative isomorphisms, both paths send
$$s\otimes(x\otimes y)\longmapsto(-1)^{bi}(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y).$$
Indeed $c$ has this pure-tensor formula by [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], preserves degrees, and $F$ is additive, so the sign can be applied before or after $c$. Equality on local tensor generators gives equality on each summand; equality on all direct-sum inclusions gives equality of cochain maps. This proves the representative shift square for every integer $a,b$, using the same extraction order over $R$ and $S$.

proof.text:
On resolving $E,G$, replace the two occurrences of $\mu$ by step 2 and use the naturality of $\kappa$ and the representative maps of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The representative normalization of $\sigma,\sigma'$ reduces the symmetry equation to
$$c_{G,E}F(\beta_{E,G})=\beta_{FE,FG}c_{E,G}.$$
This is the signed-symmetry clause of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Explicitly, on $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ of bidegree $(i,j)$ both paths have value $(-1)^{ij}(s\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes x)$, using balancing to move $s$ between the factors. Thus the representative symmetry square commutes, with its specified Koszul sign.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), total comparison; more-algebra.tex section-sign-rules, item-flip-tensor-product.

proof.text:
On resolving $E,G,J$, use the iterated resolving totals from step 1. Expand the two occurrences of $\mu$ in each side by step 2. Naturality of $\mu$ with the inner representative isomorphism $r_{G,J}$ or $r_{E,G}$ permits replacing each inner derived tensor by its total model. Naturality of $\kappa$ and of $r,r'$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], together with the representative normalizations of $\alpha,\alpha'$, then reduces the equation to
$$(1\otimes c_{G,J})c_{E,T(G,J)}F(A_{E,G,J})=A_{FE,FG,FJ}(c_{E,G}\otimes1)c_{T(E,G),J},$$
where $A:T(T(E,G),J)\to T(E,T(G,J))$ is unsigned reassociation. This is exactly the reassociation clause of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. On a triple tensor $s\otimes((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ both paths are $(s\otimes x)\otimes((1\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes z))$. Hence the representative associativity equation holds on all direct-sum summands.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), iterated total comparison; more-algebra.tex section-sign-rules, unsigned triple reassociation.

proof.text: For each fixed $a,b$, the two sides of the shift equation are natural transformations between the same bifunctors; likewise for symmetry, and for reassociation between the same trifunctors. Their restrictions agree by steps 4–6, with all representative comparisons inserted. Apply the finite-variable full faithfulness of [lem-pur-derived-tensor-additive-constraints], with two variables for shifts and symmetry and three for reassociation. It makes these equalities hold on every tuple of derived objects and all derived morphisms. There is no boundedness condition: the resolving classes, their total tensors, and this full-faithfulness statement all concern unbounded derived categories.
